newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor's constituency probed for poll fraud.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor's constituency probed for poll fraud.

text.p: Paris prosecutors opened a probe on Friday into allegations of poll fraud in the recent parliamentary election in the constituency of the capital's conservative mayor Jean Tiberi, judicial sources said.

They said the probe followed a complaint lodged by Greens candidate Yves Fremion-Damet which was based on a newspaper report that the electoral roll in Tiberi's constituency had been padded with supporters over three decades.
There was no immediate reaction from Tiberi, who has previously denied any wrongdoing.

Gaullist Tiberi retained his seat in the National Assembly, but had to go to a runoff on June 1 against his Socialist rival Lyne Cohen-Solal. Fremion-Damet did not win enough votes in the first round to qualify for the runoff.
The election gave the left a majority in the National Assembly, sweeping the conservatives from power.
The fresh probe added to the troubles of Tiberi who is formally being investigated on suspicion that he and his wife Xaviere received a suspect payment from public funds for a report she wrote.

The satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine said before the May 25-June 1 election that up to 4,000 voters -- nearly 10 percent of the district's roll -- were illegally registered there despite living elsewhere.
Le Canard said many of those voters had simply failed to report that they moved out of the district, but many others were supporters who owed city hall a favour.

Tiberi has said non-resident voters were common in all the capital's districts. "Many voters want to keep voting in a district they love...I had no need of these votes to be elected," he said before the election.
